heading: Ordering
text:
### Ordering [IRET.11.1]

The agenda is a min-heap (or sorted structure) ordered by
the comparison key `(terminal ordinal, creation_timetag)` —
lower ordinal first, and among activations of the SAME rule,
earliest-created first. Both keys are read directly off the
activation and its terminal; neither needs a lookup.

Two keys suffice, and neither has to be assumed unique. The
ordinal is unique per rule, so it separates activations of
different rules outright. Two activations of one rule share
an ordinal but cannot share a timetag, because a timetag is
assigned per token and a token reaches exactly one terminal.

**The timetag never decides between two rules**, and that is
the point: which match completed first is a property of
propagation order, and [LTES.12.9] requires the firing order
to be spec-defined rather than implementation-defined.

idris.name: iret_11_1__select
idris.note: The activation that fires next: the lowest ordinal with an unfired activation, then its earliest in timetag order. Two keys and no hash order.

idris.name: iret_11_1__select_cases
idris.note: The selection, as the two cases a proof splits on.

idris.name: iret_11_1__select_just
idris.note: What is selected is there, and unfired: the lowest ordinal with an unfired activation, its first.

idris.name: iret_11_1__select_map_just
idris.note: The selection's successor map, undone: the tail selected `(r', j)` and the whole selected `(S r', j)`.

idris.name: iret_11_1__select_nothing
idris.note: When nothing is selected, nothing is unfired: the agenda is drained.

idris.name: ldet_5_5__before_total
idris.note: The second key is a total order on one rule's live activations, so selection within a rule is determined.

idris.name: rarc_5_4_9__keys_distinct
idris.note: The second key never ties among one rule's activations.

idris.name: rarc_5_4_9__unique_after_history
idris.note: After any history, selection within a rule is by a key with no ties.

idris.name: iret_11_4__select_from
idris.note: Step 1a's lowest-ordinal search, from ordinal r on.

idris.name: iret_11_4__select_from_unfired
idris.note: The two selections agree from any ordinal on when every refracted identity is fired.

idris.name: iret_11_4__select_spec
idris.note: The spec's selection: ordinal, then the first eligible activation.

idris.name: iret_11_1__select_none
idris.note: A head terminal with no unfired activation and nothing after it selects nothing.

idris.name: iret_11_1__select_skip
idris.note: A head terminal with no unfired activation is skipped: the selection after it, one ordinal later.

idris.name: iret_11_1__select_yes
idris.note: Selection over the chains, one at a time: a head terminal with an unfired activation is selected at it.
